title: Seattle voice AI startup Ultravox, formerly known as Fixie, acquired by Inworld
key_facts: Inworld says it has acquired Ultravox, the platform developers use to build real-time voice agents.
Ultravox team members who joined Inworld will keep developing the platform.
The two firms already worked together on text-to-speech; Inworld says it brings its Realtime TTS-2 and STT-1 speech models and real-time inference infrastructure.
Built-in Inworld voices on Ultravox now run on Realtime TTS-2 at no additional cost, with no code changes needed.
Existing Ultravox customers' agents keep running as usual, with no migration required.
The blog post is dated 30 Sep 2026; Business Wire carried a release on 1 Oct 2026; GeekWire reported on 2 Oct 2026.
The post gives no price or other deal terms.
quote_evidence: Ultravox team members who have joined Inworld will continue developing the platform.
Your agents keep running as usual.
There is no migration or code change required as part of this announcement, and the TTS-2 upgrade comes at no additional cost.
why_it_matters_hint: A voice AI company buys a platform for building voice agents and upgrades its customers' voices at no extra cost.
